title: Solo Dev Uses AI to Build an Open-World RPG — Looking for Feedback on the Workflow
author: Meshyai
selftext:
I recently put together a showcase video covering a solo developer who's building an open-world RPG while heavily incorporating AI into parts of the development process.

What interested me wasn't the "AI made a game" angle, but the reality of how a solo developer can use AI tools alongside traditional workflows to tackle projects that would normally require a much larger team.

Some of the topics covered:

* Environment and world-building workflows
* Creating concept art and references before asset production
* Rapid iteration as a solo developer
* Combining AI-generated content with manual game development
* Managing scope and production on a large RPG project

One thing I'm curious about from other AI game developers:

**Where do you currently find AI most useful in your pipeline, and where does it still fall short?**

Do you see AI as primarily a prototyping tool right now, or are you actively using it in production?

I'd genuinely love feedback from people building games with AI, both on the workflow shown in the video and on how your own experiences compare.

(Video link in comments)

comments.author: teamharder
comments.body:
Obviously AI excels at wiring together actions to assets but it starts to fall apart when it's a visual aspect like UI animation or assets, the actual assets themselves. And currently the hard part is overcoming that limitation of visual inspection and interpretation of that work. I've tried some AI asset generators, including yours, and they typically fall short of human standards. They look okay for a prototype but they're not quite there for professional games. That's why I've just overall gotten more human-made assets through cheaper sources like Humble Bundle sales or Unity sales.


Overall it feels like things are accelerating towards fully polished AI games. In fact today, using the new Opus 4.8 via the MCP with Unity, it feels like another step change. I'm assuming your service will be fully viable for polished game assets within the next 6 months or so. Exciting times.

replies.author: Meshyai
replies.body: Very Exciting times! And yes, our service is ever-evolving every day. The engineers are always hard at work with the next update and it seems like, recently, there's a new breakthrough every other week.

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body: Looking forward to it. I'll keep checking back in and hopefully use it for my next game.

comments.author: just_a_timetraveller
comments.body: Looks great especially as a solo dev. What did you do for the terrain and sky textures? What is the backing engine?

replies.author: Meshyai
replies.body: Let me ask the solo dev right quick!

replies.author: Meshyai
replies.body:
LOL, the creator (the solo dev) told me he'll let me take the karma this time around, so I'll be doing the answering.



He told me that the engine he uses is Unity. For terrain, he used a plugin called MapMagic 2, which does procedural generation using graph nodes; then he would sculpt and detail by hand to get the interesting locations.



For the sky, he used the plugin called Expanse, which he says he's made numerous customizations to with Gemini to create a near fully procedurally generated sky rendering system. He also has a few links that he wanted me to share of the custom features he added to the sky rendering system.
